course.title: Atomic – Cambridge Lower Secondary Mathematics — Stage 7

unit.title: Probability
unit.blurb: The language of chance and the 0 to 1 probability scale, equally likely outcomes, mutually exclusive outcomes, and probabilities from experiments.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Use the language of chance and the probability scale from 0 to 1.

O2.t: Find probabilities of equally likely outcomes and use the fact that mutually exclusive outcomes add up to 1.

O3.t: Find experimental probabilities from repeated trials and compare them with expected results.

p: Probability measures how likely something is, on a scale from **0** (impossible) to **1** (certain). **½** is an even chance.
Words: impossible, unlikely, even chance, likely, certain.
A probability cannot be bigger than 1 or less than 0.

p: When outcomes are equally likely: **P(event) = number of ways it can happen ÷ total number of outcomes**.
Outcomes that cannot happen together are **mutually exclusive**. The probabilities of all of them add up to **1**, so **P(not A) = 1 − P(A)**.
Count ALL the outcomes in the bottom of the fraction.

req.prompt: Explain why P(not red) = 1 − P(red).

rubric.pt: a counter is either red or not red
the two probabilities add up to 1

req.model: Every counter picked is either red or not red, and these outcomes are mutually exclusive, so their probabilities add up to 1. So P(not red) = 1 − P(red).
req.reason: Every counter picked is either red or not red, and these outcomes are mutually exclusive, so their probabilities add up to 1. So P(not red) = 1 − P(red).

p: **Experimental probability** = number of times an event happens ÷ number of trials.
The **expected** number = probability × number of trials. A fair coin tossed 50 times: expect about 25 heads. More trials give a better estimate.
Experimental results are not always exactly what you expect.
